Make a microgame for this request:
a spooky wizard school mystery where my roommate gets framed for stealing something and I have to find the real thief before dawn

Brief: Investigate a theft in your first term at a magic academy, gather clues and name the thief at a dawn tribunal
Audience: teens and adults who like cozy fantasy and whodunits. Mood: mysterious, cozy, witty. Energy: low. Competition: light.

Reply with the complete authoring manifest, starting with "design".

{"design":{"pitch":"A snowy wizard-school whodunit: your bunkmate Wren is framed for stealing the Stormglass, and you have two bells before dawn to find the real thief.","theme":["Fernhallow","the Stormglass","Prefect Finch","Wren","Professor Thistlewood","Headmistress Ravel","the Weather Tower","Gloam’s boot room","a silver-stitched glove","lantern-fish"],"verb":"Read each scene’s four short lines, then tap one of up to three choices; a choice can add a clue to your notebook, raise or lower Trust, or unlock a later option.","twist":"Midnight only lets you visit two of three places (the Weather Tower, Wren in the Infirmary, the Prefects’ Study), your house (Cinder, Quill or Moss) unlocks its own moves, and the ‘theft’ turns out to be a cracked glass leaking winter.","arc":["Scenes 1–2: in the Great Hall you pick a house, then CRACK, the Stormglass is gone and Prefect Finch blames Wren; stand up for her, study the frost, or nod along.","Scenes 3–7: from the Midnight Corridor you visit two of three places, collecting clues (glove, crack, ledger, lantern, alibi, flinch, match); Quill can read the ward-runes and follow the meltwater to the Stormglass in the Gloam Boot Room.","Final scenes: at the Dawn Tribunal, Headmistress Ravel says ‘Name the thief’ (Prefect Finch, Wren or Professor Thistlewood), or, in the boot room, you take the glass to the tribunal, mend it yourself, or fetch Wren to mend it."],"lose":"Five of the 7 endings are bad and end the run 5 seconds after they appear: accuse Finch with fewer than 3 clues (All Hunch, No Proof), accuse Wren (The Wrong Friend) or Thistlewood (Slander in the Staffroom), mend the glass yourself (The Snowman), or keep a pocket summer (Pocket Summer).","win":"Accuse Finch with 3 or more clues for Case Closed (+500), or reach the secret Weather Menders ending (+900): Quill reads the runes, Trust is 2 or more so Wren can mend the glass, and you return it before dawn. Score = Clues × 100 + Trust × 50 + Ending, shown on the end card.","juice":["A clue: the sparkle sound, 18 frost-blue particles burst from the toast line, the Clues pill pops and a gold toast names it: ‘Clue: a silver-stitched glove’.","Trust gained: a chime, 10 gold particles and the Trust pill pops with ‘Wren will remember that’ (losing Trust bonks, shakes 4 px and buzzes a warning haptic).","A good ending: 40 frost-blue particles drift up from the vignette as ‘THE END’ fades in over the score line and ‘One of 7 endings. Try another path.’"],"look":"A candlelit gothic academy at midnight: a gold-traced pointed arch over deep indigo stone with drifting frost-blue snow; indigo, candle gold and frost blue feel mysterious but cozy. Each scene shows one of eight gold-framed storybook vignettes, choices sit on gold-edged indigo plaques with diamond studs, gains toast in gold and losses shake the screen. Font: Baskerville.","voice":"Wry, cozy-gothic boarding-school mystery with dry jokes at the first-year’s expense: “Her notes: ‘Storm loose! Data!’”, “Wren sniffs: ‘Apology noted.’”, “Clue: Finch flinched.
